references.text: In Matthew's parallel account of the raising of Jairus' daughter, the crowd also mocked Jesus when he said the girl was only sleeping, because they knew she had died.
Mark's parallel account describes the same scene where people laughed at Jesus, because they knew the girl was dead.
Sarah laughed when she heard the promise that she would have a son, due to her unbelief—a parallel to how the crowd mocked Jesus' words because they lacked faith.
Elisha raised the Shunammite woman's son from the dead, and the boy was clearly dead. Here too, God's power to raise the dead was revealed despite the seemingly impossible situation.
Martha protested when Jesus asked for the stone to be removed from Lazarus' tomb, because she knew he had already been dead for four days—a similar human reaction to what seemed impossible.
When Peter raised Tabitha (Dorcas) from the dead, it was clear that she had died, and those present wept. Yet God's power proved stronger than death.
